title: The Synthesis of RGD-functionalized Hydrogels as a Tool for Therapeutic Applications
protocol: Dissolve 500 mg of 4-azidobutanoic acid in 10 ml dichloromethane and 0.5 ml dimethylformamide.
Cool the solution to 0°C using an ice bath.
Add 505 μl oxalyl chloride dissolved in 5 ml dichloromethane dropwise to the reaction system while stirring.
Stir at 0°C for 1 hour, then return to room temperature.
Remove the solvent under reduced pressure using a rotary evaporator.
Characterize the obtained product by 1H-NMR spectroscopy, dissolving the sample in CDCl3.
Return to room temperature and stir overnight.
Add 1 ml of 1 M HCl.
Remove the solvent under reduced pressure using a rotary evaporator.
Dissolve 200 mg of 35% w/w PAA solution in 15 ml of distilled water.
Dissolve 15.4 mg of propargylamine hydrochloride in 15 ml of distilled water.
Dissolve 42.8 mg of HOBt in 14 ml of a 1:1 v/v acetonitrile:distilled water solution by heating to 50 °C.
Add the HOBt solution to the PAA and propargylamine solutions at room temperature.
Add 53.6 mg of EDC to the reaction mixture.
Adjust the pH to 5.5 using 1 M HCl.
Stir the reaction system overnight at room temperature.
Dissolve 11.2 g of sodium chloride in 2 L of distilled water.
Add 0.2 ml of 37% w/w HCl to the solution.
Perform dialysis for three days, changing the dialysis solution daily with 2 L of freshly prepared distilled water containing 0.2 ml of 37% w/w HCl using a membrane with a Mw cut-off of 3.5 kDa.
Store the final solution at -80 °C.
Lyophilize it according to manufacturer's protocols.
Characterize the functionalized polymer by 1H-NMR spectroscopy, dissolving the sample in D2O.
Dissolve 78 mg of PAA modified alkyne 3 in 10 ml of distilled water.
Dissolve 25 mg of the RGD azide 2 derivative in 5 ml of tetrahydrofuran.
Add all of the RGD solution to the polymeric solution.
Add 2.2 mg of copper iodide and 2.2 mg of sodium ascorbate to the mixture.
Reflux the resulting mixture overnight at 60 °C, with stirring.
Cool the mixture to 25 °C.
Dialyze the solution using a membrane with a Mw cut-off of 3.5 kDa.
Prepare a sodium chloride solution by dissolving 11.2 g of sodium chloride in 2 L of distilled water and adding 0.2 ml of 37% w/w HCl.
Perform dialysis for three days, changing the dialysis solution daily with 2 L of freshly prepared distilled water containing 0.2 ml of 37% w/w HCl.
Store the final solution at -80 °C after lyophilization according to manufacturer's protocols.
Characterize the obtained product by 1H-NMR spectroscopy, dissolving the sample in D2O.
Prepare PBS by dissolving 645 mg of PBS salt in 50 ml of distilled water.
Blend 40 mg of carbomer and 10 mg of functionalized PAA 4 with 9 ml of PBS until complete dissolution (30 min).
Add 400 mg of PEG to the solution and keep stirring for 45 min.
Adjust pH to 7.4 using 1 N NaOH.
To 5 ml of the obtained mixture, add 25 mg of agarose powder.
Irradiate the system with microwave radiation at 500 W until boiling, usually between 30 sec and 1 min.
Electromagnetically heat up to 80 °C.
Leave the mixture exposed to room temperature until its temperature decreases to 50 °C.
Add 5 ml of PBS to obtain a solution at a 1:1 volumetric ratio.
Prepare 12 multiwell plates containing steel cylinders with a diameter of 1.1 cm.
Take 500 μl aliquots from the solution and place them in each steel cylinder.
Leave at rest for 45 min until complete gelification of the system.
Remove the cylinders using a stainless steel forceps to obtain the hydrogels.
Load therapeutic tool (drug or cells) by adding 5 ml of the desired drug solution or cell culture when the mixture reaches 37 °C, obtaining a final system at a 1:1 volumetric ratio.
Soak one of the synthetized hydrogels in 2.5 ml of distilled water for 24 hours after gel formation.
Remove the aqueous media where the hydrogel is submerged and freeze-dry with liquid N2.
Add a spatula full of KBr into an agate mortar.
Take a small amount of hydrogel sample (about 0.1-2% of the KBr amount) and mix with the KBr powder.
Grind the mixture until the powder is fine and homogenous.
Use the KBr pellet kit to form the IR pellet.
Press the powder using a manual laboratory press for 3 minutes at a pressure of 5 tons.
Continue pressing the powder for an additional 3 minutes at a pressure of 10 tons.
Release the pressure to obtain a homogeneous and transparent pellet.
Insert the pellet into the IR sample holder.
Run the spectrum.
Fill a 2 ml microcentrifuge tube with 900 µl of PBS and equilibrate to 37 °C.
Add 100 µl of the prepared polymer solution to form the hydrogel.
Incubate at 37 °C.
Invert the tube and observe if the gel flows at 1, 2, 5, 10, and 20 minutes.
Record the time at which the gel does not flow as the gelation time.
